entry.title: Industrial and Systems Engineering: A day in the life

media:group.media:title: Industrial and Systems Engineering: A day in the life
media:group.media:description:
What is a day like in the life of a student in industrial and systems engineering (ISE)?
How to analyze data, improve organization, and streamline supply chains are big topics for Lauren Mullikin as a senior in the Grado Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering at Virginia Tech. Spend a day with Lauren as she works on a senior design project for a local retirement home, attends manufacturing and ergonomics classes, interns at Clorox, and leads Virginia Tech's chapter of the Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers.
Interested in industrial and systems engineering? Learn more here: https://go.vt.edu/utuyF

entry.title: Dean Warren Dixon explains why great engineers are curious

media:group.media:title: Dean Warren Dixon explains why great engineers are curious
media:group.media:description:
A new era of engineering is here, and every innovation begins with a question.
Ask Dean Warren Dixon what drives new discoveries, and he'll answer "curiosity." At Virginia Tech's College of Engineering, Hokie Engineers engage in interdisciplinary, experiential learning and groundbreaking research to tackle real-world challenges in artificial intelligence, robotics, health technologies, infrastructure, advanced materials, autonomous systems, water quality, and emerging technologies. Their questions lead to breakthroughs that create positive change in Virginia communities and around the world. And when they find an answer, they keep asking what's next.
Are you ready to discover what's next for you?
Find your answer here: https://go.vt.edu/uoJJ6

entry.title: Biomedical Engineering: A day in the life

media:group.media:title: Biomedical Engineering: A day in the life
media:group.media:description:
Virginia Tech's Department of Biomedical Engineering is full of opportunities for hands-on projects and teamwork. Spend a day with Morgan Teeters, as she studies and works through a busy spring semester. Completing a senior design project, taking a neuro-rehab class, interning with Kimberly-Clark, and leading Virginia Tech's chapter of the Undergraduate Biomedical Engineering Society are all part of Morgan's recipe for success.
Interested in biomedical engineering? Learn more here: https://go.vt.edu/uskVa

media:group.media:title: Dean Dixon welcomes Hokies
media:group.media:description:
Dean Warren Dixon welcomes Hokies from near and far to Virginia Tech Engineering.
He encourages undergraduate students to get involved in whatever way they can, especially design teams, student organizations, and helping out their local community in the spirit of Ut Prosim (That I May Serve). Over the course of earning their degree, they’ll participate in bridge experiences, like internships and co-ops, designed to prepare them for the workforce. Of course, students are encouraged to seek help from faculty, staff, peers, and advisors if they need it.
Interested in learning more about Virginia Tech Engineering? Visit here: https://go.vt.edu/uoJJ6

media:group.media:title: College of Engineering Building Tour
media:group.media:description:
Virginia Tech's College of Engineering blends historic landmarks with cutting-edge facilities that power innovation, research, and hands-on learning for undergraduate and graduate students.
From the construction-focused spaces of Bishop-Favrao Hall and Hitt Hall to the advanced laboratories of Goodwin, Whittemore, and Durham Halls, each building plays a unique role in preparing the next generation of engineers. This tour highlights the diverse academic, research, and collaborative spaces found across Bishop-Favrao, Data & Decision Sciences, Drone Park, Durham, Gilbert, Goodwin, Hitt, Holden, Kelly, McBryde, Mitchell, New Classroom Building, Norris, Patton, Seitz, Torgersen, and Whittemore.
Interested in learning more? Visit here: https://go.vt.edu/uoJJ6

entry.title: Why do certain buildings survive earthquakes?

media:group.media:title: Why do certain buildings survive earthquakes?
media:group.media:description:
Is there such a thing as an earthquake-proof house? Why is it actually a good thing when certain parts of a building fail during an earthquake? What should you do to protect yourself if you're inside when the ground starts shaking?
Matt Eatherton, a professor in civil and environmental engineering at Virginia Tech, studies how buildings behave during earthquakes and how to design them to be more resilient. Using advanced computational models, lab testing, and real-world assessments, Eatherton's research helps engineering specialists design safer structures and save lives.
Want to learn more? Visit: https://go.vt.edu/up1O0

media:group.media:description:

entry.title: From concept to can: Inside ID Pro

media:group.media:title: From concept to can: Inside ID Pro
media:group.media:description:
At Virginia Tech, students in the Interdisciplinary Projects (ID Pro) program are gaining real-world experience by working directly with industry partners.
In this project, students collaborated with local company Wilderness Mountain Water, home to a rare flowing artesian water source, to tackle both engineering and branding challenges. From optimizing systems to designing a custom can and packaging for campus, students applied their skills across disciplines to bring ideas to life.
This hands-on experience connects students from the College of Engineering, Food Science & Technology, and Creative Technologies with industry early in their academic journey, helping them build professional skills, take creative risks, and prepare for future careers. By working alongside faculty and industry experts, students learn what it takes to move a concept from idea to reality.
See how collaboration, innovation, and experiential learning come together to shape the next generation of engineers and creators.
